meta: Jacob Jordaens's As the Old Sang the Young Play Pipes, an early version of a Dutch proverb he painted several times.
about: The title is a Dutch proverb, and Jacob Jordaens painted it several times. This Antwerp version, made between 1638 and 1640, is the earliest of them. A later one is in Valenciennes. Jordaens was Flemish, and the oil on canvas now belongs to the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp, known as KMSKA.

meta: A woman rides a bull with a village behind her in Utagawa Kunisada's 1836 Tokaido print Picture of Kanbara, at the Library of Congress.
about: A woman rides a bull, with a village behind her. The Library of Congress describes the scene in just those words. Utagawa Kunisada made the color woodcut in 1836 for the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, a series named after the road between Edo and Kyoto. This sheet is the one for the station of Kanbara. The print measures about 25 by 19 centimetres.

meta: An American woman plays an accordion beside a dog and a standing man in Utagawa Sadahide's Japanese print of about 1860.
about: An American woman plays the accordion in this Japanese print by Utagawa Sadahide. A dog sits at her right, and a man stands to her left. The Library of Congress holds the color woodcut, which it dates to 1860. The print was made on hōsho paper and is about 36 by 24 centimetres.

meta: A sailor wades through water carrying a soldier on his shoulder on Henry Reuterdahl's 1918 Navy recruiting poster.
about: A sailor wades through water with a soldier on his shoulder. The words on the poster say the Navy put them across, and offer the service to men from 17 to 35 for travel and training. Henry Reuterdahl made the color lithograph in 1918. It is in the Library of Congress and measures about 118 by 74 centimetres.

meta: A small red-capped bird perches on a bamboo stake beside a lily in Baison's 1890 print, held by the Library of Congress.
about: A small bird with a red cap sits on a bamboo stake that supports a lily plant. Baison made the print in 1890. The Library of Congress holds it, and the sheet is small, about 14 by 8.5 centimetres. Nothing else is described in the record, only the bird, the stake and the lily.

meta: A woman stands with a parasol on the ground and a book on women's moral education behind her in Kuniyoshi's 1843 print One.
about: A woman stands full length, facing right. A parasol lies on the ground next to her, and behind her is a book on moral education for women. Utagawa Kuniyoshi made this print in 1843 and called it One. The Library of Congress holds it. The sheet is about 36 by 24 centimetres.

meta: Pieter Bruegel the Elder's Peasant Dance, painted around 1567, looted by Napoleon in 1808 and returned to Vienna in 1815.
about: Peasants dance in this oil painting on panel by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, made around 1567. Napoleon Bonaparte's forces looted it and brought it to Paris in 1808. It was returned in 1815. Today it hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, and it has been in that city since it came back.

meta: A Polish soldier brandishes a rifle beside the Polish flag on Wladyslaw T. Benda's 1917 poster Polish Army in France.
about: A Polish soldier brandishes a rifle, and the Polish flag appears beside him. Wladyslaw T. Benda made this color lithograph in 1917 as a poster titled Polish Army in France. The Library of Congress holds it in its poster collection. The sheet is large, about 90 by 68 centimetres, and the figure and the flag are what the library's description picks out.

meta: A view of the Grand Canyon on C. Don Powell's 1938 screenprint poster for Grand Canyon National Park, at the Library of Congress.
about: This poster gives a view of the Grand Canyon. Its words call Grand Canyon National Park a free government service. C. Don Powell made the color screenprint in 1938. The Library of Congress holds it in its poster collection, and the sheet is about 48 by 36 centimetres, and the record lists only the view of the canyon.

meta: Travelers rest under thatched roofs above a valley at Hodogaya station on the Tōkaidō Road in Hiroshige's 1855 print.
about: Travelers rest beneath thatched roofs at Hodogaya, a station on the Tōkaidō Road. The view runs down a valley toward mountains in the distance. Utagawa Hiroshige made this color woodcut in 1855. The Library of Congress holds the sheet, which is about 36 by 25 centimetres, and gives it the title Hodogaya in its catalog.

meta: Steep cliffs and rock formations at Lake Hakone with Mount Fuji behind, in Utagawa Hiroshige's 1858 color woodcut.
about: Steep cliffs and odd rock formations rise at Lake Hakone, and Mount Fuji stands in the background. Utagawa Hiroshige made the color woodcut in 1858. The Library of Congress holds it and calls it The lake in Hakone. The sheet is about 36 by 25 centimetres, and its record names the cliffs, the rocks and the mountain.

meta: A woman looks back through clouds at travelers on the Tōkaidō Road in Utagawa Kunisada's 1837 View of Hara.
about: A woman looks back through clouds at travelers on the Tōkaidō Road. Fields and mountains fill the background. The Library of Congress catalogs this print as View of Hara, made by Utagawa Kunisada in 1837. It is a color woodcut, about 25 by 18 centimetres, and it belongs to the library's collection of Japanese prints.

meta: Three women stroll by the river on a cool evening in Torii Kiyonaga's print from 1785, held by the Library of Congress.
about: Three women stroll next to a river and enjoy the cool evening air. The Library of Congress thinks the river is the Sumida, and it puts a question mark on that guess. Torii Kiyonaga made the print in 1785, and the library gives it the title Cooling off near the river bank. It is part of the library's collection of Japanese prints.

meta: Actors Iwai Sagenta and Katsuyama Matagorō in a Torii Kiyonobu print of 1705, one on a veranda and one climbing the steps.
about: Two actors, Iwai Sagenta and Katsuyama Matagorō, share this print. One reclines on a veranda while the other is about to climb the steps up to it. Torii Kiyonobu made it in 1705, and it is in the Library of Congress. The record names both actors and gives them these two poses, and the title repeats their names.

meta: People crowd a pavilion and Ueno Park to view cherry blossoms in Nishimura Shigenaga's print of about 1725.
about: Many people sit in a pavilion and stroll through Ueno Park to view the cherry blossoms. The title says they are viewing them from the bank of a pond at Ueno. Nishimura Shigenaga made the print in 1725. The Library of Congress holds it in its collection of Japanese prints.

meta: The actor Segawa Kikunojō V plays the woman Koharu in a Utagawa Toyokuni print of 1818, held by the Library of Congress.
about: The actor Segawa Kikunojō V appears in the role of a woman named Koharu. Utagawa Toyokuni made the print in 1818, and it is in the Library of Congress. The sheet measures about 37 by 26 centimetres. The library's record describes the portrait in a single line, with the actor shown playing a woman's part.

meta: Pedestrians cross Mannen Bridge while boats pass and Mount Fuji rises far off, in Hokusai's Under Mannen Bridge at Fukagawa.
about: Pedestrians cross the Mannen Bridge over a river, and boats move on the water below. A person fishes from a rock. Far off, Mount Fuji can be seen. Katsushika Hokusai made the view, called Under Mannen Bridge at Fukagawa, and the Library of Congress dates this print to 1890. It is a color woodcut held by the library.

meta: Many gods in human form gather in a large room at the great shrine at Izumo in Utagawa Sadahide's 1857 print.
about: Many gods, in human form, are present in a large room at a shrine. The title places them at the great shrine at Izumo. Utagawa Sadahide made the print in 1857. The Library of Congress holds it, and the sheet is about 35 by 24 centimetres. The record describes the room and the crowd of gods but names no single figure among them.

meta: A head-and-shoulders Greek figure holding a print on Katherine Milhous's 1936 poster for a Federal Art Project exhibition.
about: A Greek figure shown head and shoulders holds a print. Katherine Milhous made this poster in 1936 for an exhibition of the WPA Federal Art Project in Pennsylvania. The Library of Congress keeps it in its poster collection. The record gives no more detail about the figure than that, and the poster's purpose was to advertise the exhibition.

meta: An antelope hunt taken from a Navajo drawing on Louis B. Siegriest's 1939 poster for the Indian Court at the Golden Gate fair.
about: An antelope hunt, taken from a Navajo drawing, fills this poster. It advertised the Indian Court exhibit in the Federal Building at the Golden Gate International Exposition in San Francisco. Louis B. Siegriest made it in 1939, and New Mexico is named in the title as the place of the drawing's origin. The Library of Congress holds the poster.
